collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager volunteers as feast taster and keeps checking every dish: keep up the good work, or let the cooks taste their own.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The village is preparing a feast, and (subject) has volunteered for the most important job of all: tasting. Every stew, every sauce, every roasted thing must be checked by (subject) "to make sure it's right." Everything has been checked several times. Some dishes have been checked so carefully that there is noticeably less of them.

choices.label: Let the Cooks Taste Their Own

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (cook), the head cook, gently takes the spoon away and gives (subject) a new job: carrying firewood. (subject) carries it with a face of deep tragedy. But when the feast begins, (cook) sets the very first bowl in front of (subject), "for all your help with the tasting." (subject) decides this is a fair outcome.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) carries on tasting, thoughtful and serious, giving notes to the cooks: "More salt." "Perfect." "Let me try that one again." By the time the feast begins, (subject.he/she) is far too full to eat a single thing. (subject.He/she) sits through the whole feast watching everyone else enjoy it, and insists it was worth it.
